title: Thuthukile Zuma - Wikipedia
content: # Thuthukile Zuma. | Chief of Staff, Department of Telecommunications and Postal Services | |. | Parent(s) | Jacob Zuma Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma |. **Thuthukile Zuma** (born 28 April 1989) is the youngest of former South African president Jacob Zuma's four daughters with ex-wife Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma. She was the chief of staff to Minister Siyabonga Cwele in the Department of Telecommunications and Postal Services, and held the distinction of being the youngest head of a minister's office ever appointed in South Africa. She then joined the State Security Agency "State Security Agency (South Africa)") as a public liaison officer for less than a year, and, after the 2014 national elections, moved to the position of chief of staff for the Department of Telecommunications and Postal Services, where she received an annual salary of almost R1 million. Zuma resigned from her position as chief of staff in December, 2015.

title: Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma - Wikipedia
content: # Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma. | Minister of Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities | |. | Minister in the Presidency "Minister in the Presidency (South Africa)") | |. | Minister of Home Affairs "Minister of Home Affairs (South Africa)") | |. She was Minister of Health "Minister of Health (South Africa)") under President Nelson Mandela, and Minister of Foreign Affairs "Minister of Foreign Affairs (South Africa)") for ten years under Presidents Thabo Mbeki and Kgalema Motlanthe. During the first term of President Jacob Zuma, she was Minister of Home Affairs "Minister of Home Affairs (South Africa)"), in which portfolio she was credited with turning around a dysfunctional department "Department of Home Affairs (South Africa)"). Under President Cyril Ramaphosa, she served as Minister in the Presidency for Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation, with responsibility for the National Planning Commission, before becoming Minister of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs, in which capacity she had a prominent and controversial role in regulating South Africa's lockdown during the COVID-19 pandemic.
